findings.claim: The changeset says 'any configured blame.ignoreRevsFile neutralised (--ignore-revs-file=)'. That holds for a configured file that exists. A configured ignore file that does NOT exist (a repository config naming .git-blame-ignore-revs before the file is committed, or a global setting carried into a repository without it) makes git blame fatal before the command-line reset applies. So the run refuses with GIT_FAILED in an otherwise valid repository. Neither -c blame.ignoreRevsFile= nor a GIT_CONFIG_COUNT override clears it (measured). The refusal is loud and names git's error, and it never mis-dates. The disclosure overstates the neutralisation; the smallest fold is one clause naming this refusal.
findings.counterexample: r6-x, git config blame.ignoreRevsFile .git-blame-ignore-revs (the file does not exist). git blame --ignore-revs-file= ...: 'fatal: could not open object name list: .git-blame-ignore-revs'. The -c form and a GIT_CONFIG_COUNT override: the same fatal. rule serve floor.json --dry-run: 'The floor records' admission instants cannot be dated: git blame of .totem/spine/authoring-ledger.ndjson line 38 (ruleId 2570e3a8e586b038) failed ...'. This machine has no global blame.ignoreRevsFile. FOLDED at 103e02ea (wording only, by the seat): the changeset's git-failure sentence names the missing ignore-list file as a loud refusal with its cure, and a following sentence names the residual no local-state defence closes, a doctored object store or a rewritten or backdated history, as the same trust the file's asOf rests on.
